title: Water, Weather, Roof
logline: Through a hard monsoon stretch on a tea estate, the same families who share tea and shelter on dry days start keeping to themselves when the rain and the cold do not let up, and everyone can feel exactly when it changes.

object.note: Object 9 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Roofs carry across: from palm thatch in the dry south to estate homes through a hard monsoon, where rain and cold change how neighbours keep company.

thread_out.thread: Conditions that shape a season lead to a fire that lasts only as long as it is fed: a crew tending a wood-fired kiln through the night until it is let go out.

requirements: A tea estate community willing to be filmed through a genuinely difficult stretch of weather
Ongoing, specific consent about what hardship is shown
Enough time in the filming window to see a real shift when weather changes

suggestions.name: A tea estate community during the south-west monsoon
suggestions.why: Hill-country tea estates have well-documented seasonal hardship tied to monsoon weather and shared worker housing.
suggestions.season_notes: South-west monsoon, roughly May to September
suggestions.verify: A specific estate and community consent must be confirmed.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Weather, food and shelter strongly shape how people feel and act, making kindness easier or harder. They are strong supports, not the whole story, and they can lead to generosity as well as to friction.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: වැස්ස, කෑම බීම හා නවාතැන මිනිසුන්ගේ හිතට හා හැසිරීමට බලවත් පිහිටක් වුවත්, ඒවා කරුණාවටත් කෝපයටත් දෙකටම උදව් විය හැකි නිසා, ඒවා පමණක් කෙනෙකුගේ ගතිය තීරණය නොකරයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Paṭṭhāna's decisive-support condition (upanissaya), which the Pradeepika calls the strongest kind of support, includes a 'natural' kind: bodily pleasure and pain, weather, food and lodging. Good weather, suitable food and lodging support bodily ease; harsh weather, poor food and lodging support bodily pain; and from these the texts show both giving and virtue, and anger, lust and conceit, arising. The Abhidhamma also counts feeling, pleasant, painful or neutral, among the faculties that govern the states arising with it.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Rain days and clear days are cut back to back; meals are made from what is on hand; people share dry space or guard it. The viewer watches tempers and generosity shift with the sky in the same families, and hears the community describe the hard season in its own words.

key_terms.en: natural decisive support (including weather, food and lodging)

lesson.caution: It does not mean 'your environment determines you': the texts call weather, food and shelter strong supports for good and bad alike, not sole causes, and no one's character is being judged.
lesson.builds_on: The old roof showed continuity made of changing parts; this film shows the same families changing with the weather, as outer conditions strongly support inner states.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
